headline: PSX rebounds, but the desk keeps a defensive read while oil stays above USD 100.
summary: Official PSX data confirms KSE-100 closed September 10 at 168,865.04, down 3,078.55 pts (-1.79%), before Business Recorder's September 11 close of 170,511.85 (+1,646.81 pts, +0.98%). The rebound matters, but it does not erase the macro setup: state/global.json still has Brent 105.66 and WTI 100.76, CPI is 11.1%, and the September 14 MPC remains a hold-or-hike event. The desk's read stays cautious: banks are the cleaner fundamental pocket, E&P has valuation support but timing risk, and live triggers are low-confidence screen names only.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: UBL and MCB screen attractive in the data layer: UBL P/E 7.11 with a 7.22% covered yield, MCB P/E 8.16 with a 9.01% covered yield. The carry backdrop remains intact while SBP sits at 11.5%, but the desk still treats the group as selective quality exposure.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas E&P
sectors.why: OGDC, PPL and POL screen cheap-to-fair with strong margins, and oil above USD 100 is book-supportive. Timing remains the issue: the sector still moved with the risk-off tape during the September 10 flush.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Higher crude prices raise inventory, working-capital and pricing-pressure risk. The desk keeps this as an avoid pocket until margin and policy visibility improve.

sectors.name: Cement, autos and leveraged cyclicals
sectors.why: CPI at 11.1%, no clear MPC easing setup, and the oil/import-cost shock all work against a broad cyclical re-rate.
